subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian author.
• Things Fall Apart is one of his most acclaimed novels.
• Achebe published the novel in 1958.
• It tells the story of Okonkwo, a warrior in a traditional Igbo village during the arrival of European colonizers.
• Some themes from Things Fall Apart are also explored in Achebe's later novel No Longer at Ease.
prompt: The student wants to introduce Chinua Achebe and his novel Things Fall Apart to a new audience. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Chinua Achebe wrote the novel No Longer at Ease after he wrote Things Fall Apart.
choices.B: Things Fall Apart, an acclaimed novel that was published in 1958, depicts the impact of European colonization on traditional Igbo society from the perspective of a Nigerian author.
choices.C: In 1958, Nigerian author Chinua Achebe published one of his most acclaimed novels, Things Fall Apart, which tells the story of Okonkwo, a warrior in a traditional Igbo village during the arrival of European colonizers.
choices.D: Some of the themes that appear in Chinua Achebe's No Longer at Ease are also explored in Things Fall Apart.

explanation:
Choice C is correct. It effectively introduces Achebe as a Nigerian author and his 1958 novel Things Fall Apart about Okonkwo, a warrior during European colonization.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. The sentence indicates that two of Achebe's novels explore similar themes; it doesn't introduce Chinua Achebe and Things Fall Apart to a new audience.
